title: Research: reconcile the Mesh Booleans plan with the crawfish flow
description: 'Figure out what we need from the Mesh booleans plan.' Research-only ticket, bounded to one session, no code. Compare two routes for the crawfish merge: (a) triangle boolean of the raw scans (CRAW-16) -> re-run quad_layout on the merged mesh -> transfer labels by provenance (CRAW-15); (b) QuadMixer-style layout-preserving merge of already-laid-out members as reconstructed in quad-layout-booleans.md and the Mesh Booleans note (retract dissolved patches to a full ring, match T-junction counts by loop cuts, re-solve only the merge region). Evaluate against: label stability (the note's worry that a global re-solve changes patch labels), texture survival, singularity budget, implementation cost given what exists (Manifold provenance from CRAW-13, no Takayama patch quadrangulation, no ILP). Deliverable: a decision note `crawfish-boolean-decision.md` next to quad-layout-booleans.md with a components list and, if (b) or a hybrid wins, drafted follow-on CRAW tickets (titles + one-paragraph scope) appended to this ticket's changes-made for the user to create. MESH-38 (explore quad-preserving boolean operations, in progress) is the general research this consumes; wait for its findings and cite them.
definition-of-done: 1. crawfish-boolean-decision.md exists with: problem statement, both routes, evaluation table, recommendation, required components with existing/missing status. 2. The LCK21a non-disk guarantee question from the Mesh Booleans note is answered with a citation. 3. Follow-on ticket drafts (if any) are listed in changes-made. 4. No source files changed.
testing-plan: 1. User review of the decision note. 2. Cross-check every 'exists' claim in the components list against the codebase paths cited.
